sugestoes.texto: AuthzClient is a public client library that is frequently shaded or repackaged, and ServiceLoader files are commonly dropped in that process, so previously-working `AuthzClient.create(...)` calls now fail with an unrelated crypto error before the client is even constructed. Guard `CryptoIntegration.init` so a missing provider does not break client creation, either by catching `IllegalStateException` and continuing or by initializing lazily when the ECDSA conversion is first needed.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).

sugestoes.texto: The cache-hit branch of `getForLogin` returns raw `IdentityProviderModel` objects from `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` without `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, so `isEnabled()` no longer reflects the linked organization's state and an org-linked IDP whose organization is disabled is reported as enabled again once the cache is warm. Wrap the resolved model on the cache-hit path with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(idp)` to match the cache-miss branches at lines 218 and 249.

issues.descricao: Claims getForLogin re-enters the caching layer by calling session.identityProviders().getById instead of idpDelegate.getById; this deliberately resolves IDs through the per-IDP cache.
Claims the cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw, non-organization-aware models; getById already wraps them.
Claims linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization never invalidates the getForLogin caches; the org provider routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update which does.
Claims resolving cached IDs one by one with getById turns login listing into N lookups; those lookups hit the per-IDP cache by design.
Claims the HashSet in cached getForLogin returns IDPs in nondeterministic order; every caller sorts the result.
Claims remove() of a nonexistent alias now dereferences null; the new login invalidation is null-safe and the other call is unchanged pre-existing code.
Claims getLoginPredicate can NPE on a null config; config is always initialized.
Claims org-specific ALL/ORG_ONLY login queries include non-public org IDPs, so the BROKER_PUBLIC gate misses invalidations; the query always requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true.

getForLogin caches all organizations under one realm/mode entry, so each new organizationId invalidates and rebuilds that entry with every previously cached search merged in, instead of caching per organization.

sugestoes.texto: An evaluation result for a different resource that carries the same scope name (such as `manage` or `view`) can match here and grant access the caller was never assigned for this client. Add the resource-id guard before the scope loop, mirroring `UserPermissionsV2` line 135.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.
Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.
Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.
ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation for every client resource of type Clients, so listing clients costs one evaluation per client resource.

On ClientRemovedEvent the AdminPermissions listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 when V1 and V2 are both enabled, so client deletion fails.
Claims that with both fine-grained authz V1 and V2 enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which now throws, so client deletion fails.
Claims the test grants CONFIGURE together with MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so addComposites may succeed because of CONFIGURE and the test would pass even if canMapCompositeRoles were broken.
Claims that under FGAP V2 the client management-permissions GET/PUT endpoints call the throwing ClientPermissionsV2 overrides and return 500.

sugestoes.texto: After the server stops blocking the address (e.g. an admin removes the `BlockedEmail` rule), the user still cannot submit because `emailValidation` returns failed from the stale `rejectedEmails` entry, and this persists for the lifetime of the controller. Clear or remove entries from `rejectedEmails` when the email input changes, or reset it when the modal is reopened.

issues.descricao: Claims the rejected-email memory stores the server-normalised email, so it never matches the raw input on retry.
Claims the 'rejectedEmails.@each' dependent key does not observe pushes of plain strings, so the rejection is not shown until the email changes.
BlockedEmail.should_block? returns nil instead of false when the email has no record.
Claims EmailValidator dropped the email format check that the old User#email_validator performed, allowing invalid emails.

sugestoes.texto: When a resource-scoped check falls back to the all-groups type resource, permissions from other group resources in the same resource server can match the expected scope and grant access to a group the caller was never granted. Mirror `UserPermissionsV2` and only accept permissions whose `getResourceId()` equals `resource.getId()` before matching scopes.

issues.descricao: Claims removing the canView filter from searchForUser lets admins see users they are not allowed to view.
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission scans group resources and evaluates permissions for each on every user search or count request.
Claims deleting a group under V2 triggers the removal listener, which calls GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims testManageGroupMembership never exercises the group-level manage-membership permission.
searchForUser no longer filters results with usersEvaluator::canView, so an admin with query access but no view permission and no group grants gets an unrestricted user list.

GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) does not fall back to canView(), and the PR dropped the canViewGlobal short-circuit, so an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission is denied (and the group filtered out of listings) for any group that has its own permission resource lacking VIEW.
Claims GroupResource management-permissions endpoints call GroupPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException, causing 500s when V2 is active.

sugestoes.texto: Since `formatCalEvent` deep-clones `calEvent` without injecting the new guests, the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` branch is unreachable, so the guests added through the dialog never get notified while existing attendees receive the "new guests added" email. Send an invite to each address in `newGuests` in addition to the existing attendee fan-out.

When the booking has no attendees or the attendees array is empty in the formatted event, this throws a TypeError inside `getNodeMailerPayload` and aborts the organizer's email. Fall back to `this.calEvent.organizer.name` when `attendees[0]` is undefined.

issues.descricao: Claims newGuests.includes(attendee.email) misroutes newly added guests whose casing differs from the stored value, but new attendees are stored with exactly the submitted string.
Suggests starting with [] instead of [""] because the empty string may cause validation issues; the empty initial field is intentional and validated.

sugestoes.texto: Every non-English message file is UTF-8 encoded, but `new PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` (lines 68/77) decodes as ISO-8859-1 while `Files.readString` in `verify()` uses UTF-8, so `bundle.getString(key)` returns mojibake for non-ASCII text and the sanitizer can produce spurious "Illegal HTML" build failures on legitimate translations. Read the bundle through an explicit UTF-8 reader with `new InputStreamReader(new FileInputStream(file), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)`.

issues.descricao: Claims santizeAnchors consumes English matcher groups without validation, so a translation with more anchor tags than the English text gets incorrect results.
Notes that normalizeValue blanks the whole choice expression, so a wrong argument index inside the choice would not be flagged.
Claims the English-file path rewrite is fragile and that a messages file without an English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException.
Notes no test covers allowed tags under POLICY_SOME_HTML, so emptying the allow-list would not fail the suite.

sugestoes.texto: A query like `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__auto])` now reaches the shard sub-request with the literal token `[$__auto]`, producing an invalid LogQL query and a failing or empty result, because `applyTemplateVariables` strips `__auto`/`__range`/`__range_s`/`__range_ms` from scopedVars (datasource.ts:1113) and only re-adds `__interval`/`__interval_ms` as literal passthroughs. Interpolate the query up front with the original scopedVars semantics (e.g. via `datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`), or add the removed `__auto`/`__range*` scopedVars to the object passed to `applyTemplateVariables` so range-vector tokens resolve on the frontend.

issues.descricao: Claims interpolating before partitioning substitutes $__range so range queries are wrongly split; applyTemplateVariables leaves $__range untouched.
Notes test coverage of the new interpolation; no issue.
Notes test coverage of shard interpolation; no issue.
The interpolation test hardcodes the number of applyTemplateVariables calls, making it brittle to unrelated splitting changes.
The new interpolation tests do not set request.filters, so passing ad hoc filters to applyTemplateVariables is untested.

sugestoes.texto: The SQL expression RCE/LFI path this PR intends to block stays reachable because the `nodes.go:159-160` branch reaches `UnmarshalSQLCommand` → `NewSQLCommand` → `sql.TablesList` (DuckDB parsing) without ever calling `enableSqlExpressions`. Enforce the same check in the `TypeSQL` branch of `nodes.go` (or in `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand`) so SQL parsing is refused regardless of the call path.

issues.descricao: enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of the sqlExpressions feature flag, so SQL expressions are rejected unconditionally.
The go-duck DB was replaced by a stub whose methods always return 'not implemented', so table parsing and SQL expression execution always fail.
Claims the rejection message says 'not implemented' though the guard is a feature-flag check.
Garbled request to update db.go to use sql.NewInMemoryDB().
Vague claim that the query interface changed and lines 96 and 100 need updating.
enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path (the flag is negated and both branches return false), so SQL expressions are rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.
Claims TablesList now calls a stub that always errors, so existing parser tests in pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go would break.

sugestoes.texto: Anonymous tagging runs on each anonymous auth, so on large instances this adds a full count over the 30-day device table to a hot path for every anonymous user request. Cache the count for a short window, or enforce the limit with a cheaper bounded query such as `SELECT 1 ... LIMIT deviceLimit+1` instead of a full `COUNT(*)`.

On retry the closure prepends the query again, producing `[query, query, clientIP, ...]` so the number and positions of bound parameters no longer match the SQL, causing the UPDATE to fail or bind the wrong values on SQLite when a lock is retried. Build the full argument slice locally inside the callback (or capture `args` read-only and construct a fresh slice each call) instead of reassigning the outer `args`.

issues.descricao: Claims ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter breaks wire dependency injection because wire.go still registers it.
Claims updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update, conflating missing or stale devices with the limit being reached.
Claims anonymous clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header.
Claims anonymous authentication now fails entirely when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, instead of the previous non-blocking async tagging.
Claims TagDevice now propagates all tagging errors instead of only the limit error, breaking callers that ignored them.
Claims updateDevice's time window is based on device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), which may not match the intended logic.
ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit parameter but is still registered as a wire provider in pkg/server/wire.go, which has no provider for int64, so wire generation or compilation fails.

ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit but is still registered as a Wire provider (with an AnonStore bind) in pkg/server/wire.go; Wire cannot supply an int64, so DI generation and the server build fail.
Claims updateDevice's RowsAffected()==0 check wrongly denies already-registered devices on MySQL because MySQL reports changed rather than matched rows.

sugestoes.texto: A user who was denied a specific dashboard or folder before it existed or before the grant landed stays denied for that exact resource for shortCacheTTL (30s), keeping newly created or regranted dashboards invisible, the opposite of this PR's goal. Either drop the denial cache for name/folder-scoped checks, make the denial TTL shorter than the permission-cache TTL and invalidate denial entries when permissions are refreshed, or at minimum still fall through to getIdentityPermissions on a deny-cache hit to confirm.

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.

sugestoes.texto:
A reminder cancelled by the non-immediate path (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` sets `cancelled: true` at emailReminderManager.ts:225 while leaving `scheduled: false`) with a `scheduledDate` 1h-72h out is never cancelled by this block, then gets picked up by `unscheduledReminders` and re-scheduled and sent, which is the exact cancelled/rescheduled email bug this PR is meant to fix. Add `cancelled: false` (or `NOT: { cancelled: true }`) to the `unscheduledReminders` where-clause so flagged reminders are never re-scheduled.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-51`

Callers such as handleNewBooking.ts:968 (reschedule) pass `immediateDelete=true` expecting the previous booking's reminder to be removed, but no cascade covers it there, so stale email reminder rows persist and can be re-processed later, and the `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` counterpart always deletes the row, making the two paths inconsistent. Delete the row before or after the SendGrid request in the `immediateDelete` branch.

issues.descricao: The booking-page reschedule path cancels email reminders with immediateDelete=true, which leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB, while the dashboard reschedule path marks it cancelled for cleanup, so the two flows are inconsistent.
Claims the code comment overstates the cancel window because the query lacks a lower bound on scheduledDate.
Claims the cron's cancel loop uses an undefined `client` variable, causing a ReferenceError.
Claims the unscheduled-reminders query re-schedules reminders marked cancelled because it lacks a cancelled filter.
Claims a hard-coded "Verification code" placeholder bypasses i18n.
Claims a hard-coded "Verify" button label bypasses i18n.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid send but neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row, leaving orphaned scheduled rows inconsistent with the non-immediate path.
Claims reminders from disabled event types are still sent and can be re-scheduled because they are only marked cancelled.
Notes the isSenderIdNeeded branch removal without reporting a problem.
The new cancelled column is nullable without a default, so existing WorkflowReminder rows get null instead of false.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row, and the callers no longer delete it, so reminder rows are left orphaned in the database.
The reschedule path cancels SendGrid email reminders immediately (immediateDelete=true) instead of flagging them cancelled for the cron, which supposedly accumulates cancelled batches.
When an email reminder is cancelled immediately on reschedule, its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so stale scheduled reminder rows are left in the database.

sugestoes.texto: Since `hasCache` ignores `delegationCredentialId` while `canDisconnect` gates on it, the "Delete cached data" action offers a `deleteCache` mutation against credentials this component otherwise treats as non-modifiable. Gate the cache branch on the same `!delegationCredentialId` condition.

issues.descricao: Claims the cache refresh writes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt while the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, so the displayed 'last updated' is never what the refresh sets.

sugestoes.texto: The caching sentinel logic in the service is now completely untested, so a regression that rebuilds conditions on every call or returns stale conditions can ship without any test failing. Re-add the caching tests using the new `Prisma.sql` expectations (first call builds the condition, second call returns an equal value), mirroring the routing service suite.

issues.descricao: Claims org-scope authorization excludes members' personal bookings for organizations without child teams because user ids are fetched only when child teams exist.
Claims removing findMany and returning Prisma.Sql breaks existing callers of InsightsBookingService.
Reports that no failure could be constructed in the changed lines.
Claims toEqual on Prisma.Sql always fails because the service builds nested Sql objects while the test expects a flat literal.

sugestoes.texto: The signature advertises that status sync participates in source-based cycle prevention, but the guard is never applied, so an inbound status webhook from integration A can still produce outbound status updates that loop exactly as the assignee case did. Either remove the unused parameter or thread `assignment_source` through the `sync_status_outbound` task into `should_sync("outbound_status", assignment_source)`.

issues.descricao: Claims to_dict() returns a raw datetime for queued that fails JSON serialization when passed as Celery task kwargs.
The assignment_source parameter was added to the abstract sync_status_outbound instead of sync_assignee_outbound, which is the method that actually receives it.
Claims concrete integrations overriding should_sync(self, attribute) will raise TypeError at the new two-argument call in sync_assignee_outbound.
Claims a malformed assignment_source_dict makes from_dict return None, so should_sync fails open and re-enables the sync cycle.
test_to_dict asserts queued is not None, which is always true because queued has a default, so the assertion verifies nothing.
Claims passing AssignmentSource.to_dict() with a raw datetime to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async fails Sentry's bad-pickle check in tests and would break under a JSON serializer.

sugestoes.texto: Because the tracker supports sparse offsets, this loop costs CPU proportional to the numeric span `max_offset - start` rather than the number of tracked offsets, so a single large gap burns CPU on every ~1s commit cycle. Iterate the sorted set of tracked offsets instead, walking `sorted(o for o in all_offsets if o >= start)` and stopping at the first offset that is missing contiguously or still outstanding.

issues.descricao: Claims queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown() are unavailable on Python < 3.13, so workers never exit on shutdown.
Claims Python's randomized str hash makes group-to-queue assignment differ across processes, breaking per-subscription ordering and letting two processes handle the same subscription concurrently.
Claims FixedQueuePool.submit leaks an outstanding offset when put() raises after add_offset, permanently blocking commits for the partition.
Claims get_stats/wait_until_empty report empty while items are still in flight because qsize drops when a worker takes an item.
Claims metrics.incr receives len(committable) as the instance argument instead of the amount, so the commit count is always 1.
The offsets_committed metric is incremented by the number of partitions being committed rather than the number of offsets, so its name misdescribes the value.
Claims factory shutdown leaves SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy commit threads running and committing after shutdown.

sugestoes.texto: `ensure_loaded!` is only defined on the `FallbackLocaleList` instance that config/initializers/i18n.rb assigns to `I18n.fallbacks`, so any environment where that initializer has not populated `I18n.fallbacks` with a `FallbackLocaleList` (the initializer file failing to load before `set_locale` runs, a reload in dev/test/console, or Rails reassigning `I18n.fallbacks`) raises `NoMethodError` on every request. Guard the call with `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! if I18n.fallbacks.respond_to?(:ensure_loaded!)`, or move the preload into the backend itself so it does not depend on a specific `I18n.fallbacks` type.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.
Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.
Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.
Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.
Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
I18n.ensure_loaded! reads and initializes @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, racing with reload!/load_locale under concurrent requests.

sugestoes.texto: OAuth2 and GitHub require the exchange `redirect_uri` to be identical to the authorize value, so omitting it makes GitHub return `redirect_uri_mismatch` with no `access_token` and the pipeline shows the generic failure page for every installation. Add `"redirect_uri": redirect_uri` to `data`, matching `OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params` (oauth2.py:273-280).

When the frontend sends `installation_id=null` (as GitHub's user-account install flow does), the literal string `"null"` passes the `is None` check, is bound as state, and is later passed to `Integration.objects.get(external_id="null")`, which always misses and routes the user to the generic "Invalid installation request." page instead of redirecting to the app installer. Treat falsy and `"null"` values as absent, e.g. `if not installation_id or installation_id == "null": return self.redirect(self.get_app_url())`.

issues.descricao: Claims the OAuth state is compared to the secret pipeline signature in non-constant time, leaking timing information.
Claims other consumers driving GitHubInstallation without the new OAuth view will always be rejected; no such consumer exists.
Claims a null reference when the github_authenticated_user state is missing; the code only compares it and returns the error page.
test_github_user_mismatch asserts only the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message, which any error path would produce.
The GitHub OAuth state parameter is compared with != instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information.
The installation sender-login mismatch test asserts only the generic error text, which state mismatch and OAuth failures also produce, so it cannot show the login check caused the rejection.
The OAuth state check in GitHub OAuthLoginView compares the callback state to pipeline.signature with a plain `!=` instead of a constant-time comparison.

sugestoes.texto: For any user whose federated storage advertises a recovery-authn-codes credential that cannot be rehydrated, or whose local credential is absent, rendering the LOGIN_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES_INPUT page throws NoSuchElementException and turns the login form into a 500. Guard the Optional and throw a controlled AuthenticationFlowException or fall back to CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES when the credential or next code is absent.

issues.descricao: Claims the recovery-code validator uses non-constant-time String.equals, leaking timing information about stored codes.
Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.
Claims Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without isPresent() can throw NoSuchElementException.
Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage providers via updateCredential, while the local path stores only hashed codes.
Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.

sugestoes.texto: If the ingest-spans schema does not require `end_timestamp_precise`, any message missing it raises `KeyError` and aborts the whole batch in the process consumer. Use `val.get("end_timestamp_precise")` with a fallback such as the message timestamp, or confirm the schema marks it required.

`span_count` receives the cardinality of the destination key `set_key` after the union, not the size of `span_key`/`parent_key` being merged, so when `set_key` already holds spans from an earlier insert (the common case for an in-progress segment) it counts those pre-existing spans and `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` evicts far more than the intended overflow, silently discarding valid recent and root spans. Derive the count from the merged key itself, e.g. `span_count = redis.call("zcard", set_key)` after the unions (or subtract the prior `zcard(set_key)` from the `zunionstore` result) before deciding how many to pop.

issues.descricao: Claims the redirect-resolution limit was silently cut from 10000 to 1000, so segment trees deeper than 1000 are no longer joined, and the comment still mentions 10k.
Claims a non-root span whose key equals the resolved set key unions the key with itself and then unlinks it, deleting the buffered segment.
Claims a span message missing end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and aborts the whole batch.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch passes cursor.offset directly into queryset slicing when advanced features are enabled.
Claims BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset to an unclamped offset for previous-page cursors, allowing negative slicing.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies floor/ceil to a datetime key, raising TypeError.
Claims accessing organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError when organization_context is None.
process_batch indexes end_timestamp_precise directly, so a span without the field raises KeyError and fails the whole consumer batch.

sugestoes.texto: `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (line 578), not on `PRCommentWorkflow`, so this static reference raises `AttributeError` whenever the helper runs and breaks the title-truncation feature entirely. Reference `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)`, or move `_truncate_title` next to the workflow helpers.

issues.descricao: Claims the unauthenticated endpoint iterates an unbounded array of reports, allowing CPU/metric-spam DoS.
Claims BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns Django HttpResponse objects although its Endpoint base expects DRF Response objects.
The assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, so requests rejected with 404 are still counted as assemble events, skewing analytics.
BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update() reads validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of 'type', so detector type changes are silently ignored.
Claims get_condition_query_groups indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] and may KeyError for a DCG missing from the precomputed map.
Claims the triggered_actions log now writes the full event payload with user data because event_data was switched to workflow_event_data.
Claims the success path dereferences data.summary without guarding undefined data when the query is disabled or errored.
Claims the column fallback crashes when tableData is defined but meta is missing.
Claims ExploreParams still reads visualize.yAxes after the Visualize class switched to yAxis, producing undefined saved-query params.
Asks to verify that no caller passes Visualize instances instead of BaseVisualize to updateLocationWithAggregateFields.
Claims the number-type test's mock matches query.query instead of substringMatch, so its not-called assertion can never fail.
Claims the attribute key is interpolated into the request path without encodeURIComponent, enabling path confusion.
get_environment_info fetches the recommended event per issue while building the merged-PR comment, an N+1 lookup on the comment path.
The number-type test mock matches on query.query while the hook sends substringMatch, so the mock can never match and the not-called assertion cannot fail.

sugestoes.texto: Now that each process budgets against only its own shards through `shard_factor = len(self.assigned_shards)` (buffer.py:382-384), the effective per-cycle flush ceiling is multiplied by the process count, pushing simultaneous Redis reads and Kafka produce volume beyond what `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` was sized for. Divide the configured budget across processes, for example by passing a per-process budget to `SpansBuffer` or scaling `max-flush-segments` by `num_processes`, so the cluster-wide ceiling stays constant.

issues.descricao: Splitting the buffer per process makes spans.buffer.max-flush-segments a per-process cap, so with P flusher processes up to P times the configured segments are loaded and flushed per cycle.
Claims the CLI default of 1 makes the one-process-per-shard auto mode unreachable.

sugestoes.texto: Any write events arriving between the search watcher starting and `initWatcher` subscribing are consumed by the search reader but never reach the broadcaster, so Watch subscribers silently miss those changes. Subscribe the broadcaster by calling `initWatcher` before starting the search event-draining goroutine, or have both consume from a single shared event source.

issues.descricao: Claims the new postgres t.Skip removes coverage of the storage-server instrumentation test for that backend.
Claims making NewResourceServer call Init changes the constructor contract, blocking on the full index build and failing construction on any index error.
Claims starting the watcher after search.init makes writes between the index snapshot and initWatcher never reach the search index.
NewResourceServer now runs Init synchronously and fails construction on init error, blocking on index build and watcher startup and changing the constructor contract for callers.

NewResourceServer now runs Init synchronously (lifecycle, full search index build, watcher) and returns an error on failure, so callers that were not changed block on startup and abort construction on Init failure.
